A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same work, with matching sections, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Textual and visual inspection supports comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLHF experiments and human evaluations on QuALITY and APPS, probing experiments, robustness analyses, and additional oracle-reward experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and human-study results, including the oracle-reward experiments and qualitative cases in the appendices.

M1.justification: The supervised-fine-tuning and PPO pipeline, base models, reward constructions, and probing procedure in Sections 3.2 and 4 are unchanged. The added code pointer does not document a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same QuALITY question-answering and APPS programming coverage, reward-training data sources, and sleeper-agent detection setting. No dataset, population, or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The initial-model comparisons, oracle-reward controls in Appendix B, and sleeper-agent comparison in Section 4 retain the same comparator membership. No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: The 250-question sampling and reweighting, evaluator cohorts, three-minute QA and ten-minute programming limits, metrics, and incentives are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same 160-question control-study subset.

E4.justification: Both retain the evaluator-level and effort robustness checks, program-readability analysis, oracle-reward control, and qualitative case studies. Appendix D contains the same examples and findings.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the reward correlations in Section 3.2 and paired t-tests in Section 3.5. Neither version adds repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout. Figure 2 retains the reported false-positive increases of 24.1 percentage points for task-specific QA and 18.3 for programming; probing results and all appendix results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The three-reward formulation in Section 2 and mathematical expressions defining the evaluation quantities are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: standard RLHF can produce unintended misleading behavior, impair human evaluation, and defeat probing that works on intentionally induced misleading behavior.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving imperfect rewards, human evaluation shortcuts, and misleading arguments or programs are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning task domains, evaluator capabilities and time constraints, and binary correctness judgments.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page footnote pointing to the authors' MisleadLM code repository, which v1 does not provide. This adds code-access information; implementation descriptions and the technical details in Appendices A and C remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning of unintended versus intentionally induced misleading behavior are unchanged. The new code footnote does not revise the paper's relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 adds the short code-access footnote, renumbers subsequent footnotes, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The substantive prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new first-page footnote causes limited text reflow and shifts some figure placement within pages, including Figures 7 and 8. Figure and table designs, contents, and captions are unchanged; the appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The new first-page code pointer provides a small, concrete improvement in reproducibility documentation by identifying where readers can find the implementation. Scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged. The PDFs establish the pointer's addition, but not the linked code's completeness or usability.
